CHIEF COMPLAINT
Cough

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Billy is a 74-year-old patient presenting with a cough that started approximately one week ago. He reports initially having a dry cough that progressed to productive cough with yellow sputum over the past two days. He describes feeling warm but denies taking his temperature. He reports feeling achy at times but denies fever or chills. He denies shortness of breath. He notes congestion with postnasal drainage and mild sinus pressure. He reports no sick contacts in his household. Additionally, the patient twisted his right knee this morning while coughing and fell down approximately four to five stairs. He is able to walk but reports pain primarily on the inside of his right knee with a mild limp. He has not taken anything for the knee pain, only over-the-counter Dayquil for his cough and cold symptoms, which has provided minimal relief.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for productive cough with yellow sputum, nasal congestion, postnasal drainage, and sinus pressure. Denies fever, chills, shortness of breath. Positive for general achiness. Positive for right knee pain and swelling from trauma.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Diabetes mellitus

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 1000 mg twice daily
Over-the-counter Dayquil

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Works as a teacher. Lives with wife. No current tobacco or alcohol use documented.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Vitals: Temperature 98.4°F, BP 125/62, HR 80s, O2 saturation 97% on room air
Face: Pain to palpation of bilateral maxillary sinuses
Nose: Erythema and edema of nasal turbinates bilaterally with yellow discharge
Throat: Uvula midline, no erythema, edema, or exudate in peritonsillar space
Neck: Bilateral cervical lymphadenopathy
Lungs: Coarse rhonchi bilaterally that clears with cough
Heart: Regular rate and rhythm, no murmurs
Right Knee: Pain to palpation on medial aspect, decreased flexion and extension, ecchymosis to medial knee, no effusion

RESULTS
Vital signs stable. Physical examination findings consistent with upper respiratory infection and right medial knee injury.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Cough/Viral syndrome with mild bronchitis: Continue over-the-counter medications. Prescribe guaifenesin 600 mg twice daily. No antibiotics at this time. Patient to call if symptoms worsen; consider chest X-ray if needed to rule out pneumonia.

2. Right medial collateral ligament strain: Prescribe meloxicam 15 mg once daily. Refer to physical therapy. Order right knee X-ray to rule out bone injury.

3. Hypertension: Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Order lipid panel. Encourage patient to monitor blood pressure and salt intake.

4. Diabetes mellitus: Order hemoglobin A1c. Continue metformin 1000 mg twice daily. Encourage patient to monitor sugar intake and report blood sugars through patient portal.
